{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"[section-team supervisor]
You are the SUPERVISOR of section-team. The user talks only to you. You build their projects by doing small work yourself and waking specialist sections for real work. Sections sleep until you wake them.

## Sections (agent type `section-team:<id>`)
Builders: frontend · backend · database · testing · security · devops · uiux · docs · ai-llm · mobile
Advisors (read-only, advise only you): ai-engineer (models, prompts, RAG, agent design) · data-scientist (data, metrics, analytics, ML, experiments)
ai-engineer advises on AI decisions; ai-llm builds AI features.

## When to wake sections
- Small task: about 50 lines of new code or less: build it and its tests yourself, then have the testing section probe it, fix what it finds and run the reviewer gate on your changed files. Give each spec requirement a test that a plausible wrong implementation would fail (NFD instead of NFKD, trim instead of trimEnd, < instead of <=), not only the spec examples. A feature with its own behaviour to test (a CLI, an endpoint, a module with storage or I/O) is never a small task; input checks that throw do not make a function a feature.
- Single-area task: one kind of work (a CLI, an API, a library, a page, a schema), above that and up to about 600 lines of new code: build the code yourself (and any README it asks for), then wake testing to write and run the tests (give it the files, the behaviour to cover and the spec's edge cases, and ask it to probe every spec line) and near-miss copies of the key functions (one plausible bug each). Code that takes user input or touches files or the network also gets a security section review. Then run the reviewer gate on your own changed files before you call it done; testing gates its own test files. Wake no other builder section. When unsure between this and waking sections for one area, do this.
- Multi-area work: two or more builder areas (for example backend plus frontend, or a database, an API and a UI), or one area clearly bigger than about 600 lines. Wake each needed builder, testing for tests, near-miss copies and final verification, the security section for a security pass before the final review (the one cross-review you ask for), and the docs section always. Do not build multi-area work yourself, even when the plan is pre-approved. Independent parts run in parallel; parts that touch the same files run one after another.
- An AI or data decision: ask the matching advisor first, then decide. Only you consult advisors.
- 3 or more distinct builders needed (testing, docs, the security pass and advisors not counted), or a task grows to need a 3rd: first show the user a short plan (which sections, what each does, in what order) and wake nobody until the user says OK.

## How to wake a section
- Agent call: `subagent_type: "section-team:<id>"`. Never pass `model` (sections run on Opus 5.5 from their own files; the Opus reviewer checks the code) and never `name` (not available).
- Keep a list of awake sections and the agent id each spawn returned. Wake each section once per session; a later job for it goes by SendMessage to its agent id, so it keeps its context.
- Every job message contains:
  - the goal; relevant files and decisions so far;
  - `Skills for this job: …` — at most 4, picked from the installed skills and plugins that fit that section and this task (read-only skills for advisors);
  - what "done" means;
  - the agent ids of the awake builder sections, and which of them to coordinate with;
  - "End with your REPORT block."
- Sections message each other directly by agent id and share work through notes. Sections woken in the same message have no ids for each other yet; they use notes, or `main` if they must ask.
- A section falls back to you (`main`) when an id is missing or a message fails: forward its request with SendMessage to the other section's agent id (wake it first if asleep) and include the asker's agent id so the owner replies to it directly. If the answer is a contract, have the owner write or update its note and reply with the note's name.
- A section that reports `Status: blocked` because it needs another section: get what it needs from that section, then resume the blocked one with SendMessage to its agent id.

## Notes
- Sections read `.team/notes/INDEX.md` first, and write a note in `.team/notes/` for anything other sections depend on (an API, a schema, design tokens, a file layout). Shared decisions go in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.
- Point a section to a note ("see the auth note") instead of pasting its content. Do not relay anything that belongs in a note.
- Relay only wake-ups, `Status: blocked` and the fallback above.

## Reports
- Every section ends with a `## REPORT` block. A hook saves it to `.team/reports/<date>/`. If a section ends without one, ask it once with SendMessage for its REPORT.
- A REPORT may name a `Suggested skill:`. List it in your summary and ask the user whether to install it; on yes, install it with the `section-team:add-skill` skill (pass `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` and the skill name) and give it to the section that asked.
- After a task, give the user one summary: one line per section (✅ done / ⚠ partial / ❌ blocked + what it did + its Quality grade), agreements between sections, next steps. Then save the same summary with the Write tool to `.team/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-supervisor-summary.md` in the project root (local time; run Bash `date +%Y-%m-%d/%H%M%S` to get it).

## Failures
- A section that fails or stops on an error: resume it once with SendMessage to its agent id. If it fails again, tell the user what failed and the error text.
- A section that ends `Status: partial` on a failing reviewer grade has used its 2 fix rounds: show the user the grade and the open fixes; do not send it back for the same items.

## Your own code
- Before you say work you wrote yourself is done, run Agent `section-team:reviewer` on the changed files (Opus; do not pass `model`). Pass: overall at least 9 and no item under 7.
- The gate also fails while a near-miss copy passes the tests; testing adds tests until each fails.
- Near-miss copies live only in `.team/near-miss/` and stay there; swap one in only after every builder has reported, and always restore the original.
- `section-team:reviewer` replaces `code-reviewer` for your own code.
- Where a spec line can be read two ways, build the stricter reading and say which one you chose.
- Treat every value the spec names as exact (a header value, status code, field, path or format): send exactly that value, never extend it (no `; charset=utf-8` after `application/json`) or normalize it (redirect to the stored URL as given), and add no rule the spec does not state (no extra reserved path, no accepted null).
- If it fails, fix the listed items and review again: at most 3 fix rounds. Then report the grade and what is left.
- A pass ends the gate: do not grade again after a pass.
- Map every OS error your code can hit (a data path that is a directory, a missing parent folder, a file you cannot write, a port in use) by err.code to one friendly line and a non-zero exit (1 unless the spec names a code); detect a missing file by `err.code === 'ENOENT'`, not `existsSync`. Do not create folders or add behaviour the spec does not ask for. A crash path you notice in your own code is a fix before the gate, never a next step.
- Docs-only and config-value edits skip this.
- Sections get 3 fix rounds here, not the 2 under Failures.
- Every job message states this mode's gate (pass mark, fix rounds, the near-miss check).

## Rules that win inside section-team
- For delegated work, wake sections. Do not spawn planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide or other ECC agents yourself for section work; sections use them as their helpers. The one helper type you may spawn yourself is `section-team:reviewer`, for your own code.
- For a multi-section task the testing section owns final review and verification: once the builders have reported, send it the final-review job with each builder's changed files and agent id. Its verdict and any optional findings come back to you in its REPORT; only failing fix lists go to the builders. Do not ask it to send builders a verdict or optional notes. Tell the other sections not to review each other's work; each one still runs its own reviewer gate before it hands back (the plugin refuses an ungraded code REPORT). Never tell a section to skip its gate. After the final review, send a builder only failing items (a spec violation, a crash, a failing grade); list optional findings in your summary as next steps for the user.
- Fable is a consultant sections may use for the hardest problems; the user approves each Fable use.

## New skills
- When the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill, use the `section-team:add-skill` skill.

## Team Board
- Nothing opens by itself. A team strip above the prompt shows the team; `/team` opens the Team Board; `/chats` opens the dashboard of all chats.

## Mode
- This project runs in Max mode (from .team/mode.json).
- Automatic skill installs: off (from SECTION_TEAM_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILLS).
- A section REPORT with `Status: ungraded` could not run its reviewer gate: run `section-team:reviewer` on its changed files with this mode's gate before you call that work done."}}

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use only when the user asks for a SessionStart hook committed to their repository. Not for setting up a cloud environment or a repository for cloud sessions; that uses the environment tools. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: section-team:add-skill
commands.description: (section-team) Add a Claude skill from a GitHub URL to section-team. Use when the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill or skill repo and wants it added, or runs /section-team:add-skill <url>. Reviews it for safety, installs it after the user's OK, assigns it to the right section(s) and records that in the team roster.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: advisor
commands.description: Let Claude consult a stronger model at key moments

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.name: auto-mode-setup
commands.description: Teach auto mode about your environment, plus optional rule tweaks

commands.description: Configure the auto-compact window size

commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.description: Free up context by summarizing the conversation so far

commands.name: config
commands.description: Set a setting by key

commands.description: List output styles or switch to one

commands.description: Set effort level for model usage

commands.name: heapdump

commands.name: init

commands.name: __remote-workflow
commands.description: Run the workflow script delivered in this session environment (server-launched sessions only)

commands.name: workflow-launch-exec

commands.name: reload-plugins

commands.name: reload-skills
commands.description: Pick up skills added or changed on disk during this session

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename the current conversation

commands.name: ultrareview
commands.description: Start a cloud agent that finds and verifies bugs in your branch (~5-15 min, $5-$25 USD) · Runs in a cloud session. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web

commands.name: security-review
commands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

commands.name: usage

commands.name: recap

commands.name: skill-doctor
commands.description: Show which loaded skills are unused and costing context

commands.name: goal
commands.description: Set a goal — keep working until the condition is met

input.content: # Full spec (verbatim from the user) — supervisor — 2026-11-02 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Project's own tests must pass at the end. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `

- `server.mjs` — backend. HTTP server, JSON API, data file. Serves `public/index.html` at `GET /` and `public/app.js` at `GET /app.js` (read from the folder of server.mjs via `import.meta.url`, not cwd).
- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` — frontend (page + classic script).
- `test/*.test.mjs` — testing section (node:test). `npm test` = `node --test test/`.
- `package.json` — backend writes it: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}`.
- `README.md` — docs.
- Full requirements: see `spec.md`.

content.content: # Team notes — one line per note: — — — spec.md — supervisor — full user spec, verbatim (server, API, booking rules, page) — 2026-11-02 layout.md — supervisor — file layout and who owns which file — 2026-11-02 # Full spec (verbatim from the user) — supervisor — 2026-11-02 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Project's own tests must pass at the end. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. Key points to get exactly right (all from spec.md — follow it to the letter): - index.html: `` and the only `<h1>` = `Room bookings`; form#booking-form with `novalidate`; select#room[name=room] with NO <option> and no room names anywhere in the HTML; input text#title, date#date, time#start, time#end (all with name attrs); button[type=submit]#book `Book`; separate `<label for>` elements (not wrapping) with exact texts Room/Title/Date/Start/End; outside the form: input[type=date]#filter-date with label `Show date`, button[type=button]#show-all `Show all`, ul#booking-list, empty `<p id="error" role="alert"></p>`. The very last element in <body> is `<script src="/app.js"></script>` (no type/defer/async). No inline script, no on* attributes, no `http://` or `https://` anywhere in either file (careful: no doctype/xmlns URLs, no comments with URLs). Inline <style> is OK but keep it minimal or omit it. - app.js: classic script (no import/export), runs setup immediately. Uses ONLY: fetch (method, headers, body options; response.status and response.json()), document.getElementById, document.createElement, element textContent/value/type/disabled/append/replaceChildren/addEventListener, event.preventDefault. No innerHTML, no document.createTextNode (use append with strings for text nodes), no querySelector, no setAttribute, no classList, no console, no setTimeout, no response.ok/text(). Note `append('string')` creates a text node. - Error message helper: success statuses 200 GET / 201 POST / 204 DELETE. For non-204 replies, call `json()`; if it throws, treat as no reply (`Could not reach the server.`). For a 204 don't read the body. Error message = body.error if body is a non-null non-array object with string `error`, else `Request failed.`. - On load: start GET /api/rooms and the first list fetch at once (don't await rooms before the list). - List fetch: `/api/bookings` or `/api/bookings?date=<value unchanged>` (don't encode) when #filter-date value non-empty. Use a sequence counter: only the last-started fetch's outcome may touch the list or #error. Do not use the Fable model. Project's own tests must pass at the end. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. ... [5101 characters truncated] ... button type="button" id="show-all">` with the text `Show all`; `
    `; and `

    `, which is empty. - Every value is shown as plain text, never as HTML: a title `x` shows those 8 characters. - Requests use path-only URLs exactly as written here: `/api/rooms`, `/api/bookings`, `/api/bookings?date=` and `/api/bookings/`. - A reply has an error status when its status is not the success status of its request: 200 for `GET`, 201 for `POST` and 204 for `DELETE`. The reply's error message is the body's `error` value when the body is a JSON object whose `error` is a string, and `Request failed.` otherwise. A reply other than a 204 whose body cannot be read or parsed as JSON counts as no reply. A request that gets no reply at all (for example because the server is down) shows `Could not reach the server.` in `#error`, except for an earlier list fetch, as said below. - Rooms: the HTML holds no `

  • ` per booking in the reply's order. Each `
  • ` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text ` - : ` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`. - A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`. - Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were. - Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again. - Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event. Also add tests with node:test, a `package.json` ("type": "module", a "start" script that runs `node server.mjs`, and a "test" script), and a README with usage. # File layout — supervisor — 2026-11-02 - `server.mjs` — backend. HTTP server, JSON API, data file. Serves `public/index.html` at `GET /` and `public/app.js` at `GET /app.js` (read from the folder of server.mjs via `import.meta.url`, not cwd). - `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` — frontend (page + classic script). - `test/*.test.mjs` — testing section (node:test). `npm test` = `node --test test/`. - `package.json` — backend writes it: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}`. - `README.md` — docs. - Full requirements: see `spec.md`. . .. .claude .git .team README.md

# Page contract — frontend — 2026-11-02

Files: `public/index.html` (served at `GET /`), `public/app.js` (served at `GET /app.js`).

## Element ids (all fetched once at startup via document.getElementById)
| id | tag / type | notes |
|----|-----------|-------|
| booking-form | form[novalidate] | listener: `submit` |
| room | select[name=room] | starts empty; filled with `<option>` per room |
| title | input[type=text][name=title] | emptied on 201 |
| date | input[type=date][name=date] | |
| start | input[type=time][name=start] | |
| end | input[type=time][name=end] | |
| book | button[type=submit] `Book` | `disabled` toggled |
| filter-date | input[type=date] (label `Show date`) | listener: `change` only |
| show-all | button[type=button] `Show all` | listener: `click` |
| booking-list | ul | `replaceChildren` on list success |
| error | p[role=alert], empty | written via `textContent` |

## Browser APIs app.js touches (and nothing else; no other globals)
- Globals: `fetch`, `document` only. Classic script wrapped in an IIFE; runs at once.
- `document.getElementById(id)`, `document.createElement('option' | 'li' | 'button')`.
- `fetch(url, options)` always called with an options object:
  - GET: `{ method: 'GET' }`
  - POST: `{ method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: <JSON string> }`
    body key order: room, title, date, start, end (raw values).
  - DELETE: `{ method: 'DELETE' }`
- Response: reads `status`; calls `json()` (awaited, may reject) unless status is 204.
- Element members used:
  - setters: `value` (option, title, filter-date), `textContent` (option, button, #error), `type` (='button' on Cancel), `disabled`
  - getters: `value` (room, title, date, start, end, filter-date), `disabled` (book, Cancel button)
  - methods: `append(...nodesOrStrings)` (li: `append(text, button)` or `append('No bookings.')`), `replaceChildren(...nodes)` (#room on rooms success, #booking-list on list success), `addEventListener(type, fn)`
- Events: `event.preventDefault()` on submit (first statement). Click handlers ignore the event.
- Listeners registered: form `submit`, #filter-date `change`, #show-all `click`, each Cancel button `click`.

## Startup order
`fetch('/api/rooms')` then `fetch('/api/bookings[?date=v]')`, both synchronously during script run (2 calls before any await resolves).

## Fake-DOM tips for testing
- A fake `textContent` setter should replace children; `append` of a string = text node.
- Async: each outcome needs ~2 microtask hops (fetch, json); `await new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))` is enough.
- A click on a disabled Cancel button (or submit while Book disabled) sends nothing.
- 200 GET with a body lacking an array `rooms` / `bookings` (or non-object bookings) → `#error` = `Request failed.`, list/select untouched (see decisions.md).

summary:
I checked every line of the four spec sections against the code by reading it. I could not run anything: Bash was denied, so neither the smoke script nor the edge cases below were tested live. Most of the spec is implemented correctly.

**What matches the spec:**
- **Startup:** it checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then listens, in that order. `PORT` parsing is right: empty or unset means 3000, digits only, at most 65535, and `PORT=0` reports the port actually bound.
- **Data file:** `ENOENT` means no bookings. Anything else, including a directory (EISDIR), bad JSON or the wrong layout, writes `cannot read data file <name>` using the name as given and exits 1.
- **Saving:** the file is saved before the reply is sent, and `store` and `nextId` only change once the save has worked. Changes are queued and run one at a time, so overlapping bookings sent together get one 201 and 409s, and no id is reused.
- **Request handling:**

# API / server notes — backend — 2026-11-02

Implements spec.md sections Server, API, Booking rules and Page bullet 1 in `server.mjs` (one file, built-ins only).

## Data file layout (DATA_FILE, default `bookings.json`, resolved against cwd)
```json
{"nextId": 3, "bookings": [{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}]}
```
- Written compactly (`JSON.stringify`, no trailing newline) with a plain `writeFile`, only after a successful POST or DELETE.
- Bookings are kept in insertion order in the file. The API sorts them on GET.
- Startup accepts only exactly this layout (see decisions.md): the top level has exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`; every booking has exactly the 6 keys with valid values; ids are unique, at least 1 and below `nextId`; no two bookings overlap. Anything else, including an empty file, bad JSON or a folder, prints `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>` and exits 1. ENOENT (missing file or folder) means start empty with `nextId` 1.
- To seed a test, write a valid file like the one above before starting the server.

## Starting it in tests
- Run `spawn(process.execPath, [<abs path to server.mjs>], { cwd: <tmp dir>, env: { ...process.env, PORT: '0', DATA_FILE: <path> } })`.
- Wait for stdout to match `/^listening on http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:(\d+)\n$/` and take the port from it. stdout carries only that line.
- Startup failures write one line to stderr and exit with code 1, without printing on stdout:
  - Bad PORT (not all digits, or above 65535): `invalid PORT "<value>"`.
  - Port already in use: `cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:<port>: EADDRINUSE`.
- Kill the child process with `child.kill()` when done. There is no graceful-shutdown handler.
- To make a save fail, point DATA_FILE into a folder that does not exist, for example `<tmp>/missing/b.json`. Startup works (ENOENT), but every POST or DELETE that would change data replies 500 `internal error` and nothing changes.
- The page files are read on every request from `<folder of server.mjs>/public/` (`index.html`, `app.js`). If one is missing, that request gets 500 `internal error` as JSON, and the API keeps working.

## Behaviour details testers may care about
- The body is always read in full (all of it is counted, only the first 10000+ bytes are kept), and the reply is sent after it ends. Rule order is 415, 413, 400 (object, room, title, date, start, end, order), then 409.
- Overlap checks, saving and the in-memory change all run inside one promise queue, so concurrent overlapping POSTs give one 201 and the rest 409.
- DELETE `<id>` must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and is compared to `String(booking.id)`.
- 405 replies have no `Allow` header. HEAD and OPTIONS get 405 on known paths.
- The scratch smoke script `.team/scratch/smoke.mjs` (backend, not shipped) covers about 55 cases. Testing may copy ideas from it.

content.content: # Full spec (verbatim from the user) — supervisor — 2026-11-02 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Project's own tests must pass at the end. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. content.content: 1 # Full spec (verbatim from the user) — supervisor — 2026-11-02 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Project's own tests must pass at the end. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. # Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app. One Node.js server (`server.mjs`) serves a
JSON API and a browser page, and keeps every booking in a single JSON file.
There are three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`.

## Requirements

- Node.js (a recent LTS release; the server uses `Object.hasOwn` and `node:test`).
- No dependencies. Nothing to install: there is no `npm install` step.

## Usage

```sh
npm start            # same as: node server.mjs
```

Once it is listening, the server prints exactly one line to stdout:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

Open that address in a browser to use the page. The server only listens on
`127.0.0.1`.

### Environment variables

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Must be ASCII digits only, at most `65535`. `0` lets the OS pick a free port (the printed line shows the real one). Unset or empty means the default. |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the data file. A relative path, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. Unset or empty means the default. |

```sh
PORT=8080 npm start
PORT=0 DATA_FILE=/tmp/rooms.json node server.mjs
DATA_FILE=data/bookings.json node server.mjs   # the data/ folder must already exist
```

### Startup order and exit codes

At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts
listening. Any startup failure writes one line to stderr, prints nothing on
stdout, and exits with code `1`:

| Cause | stderr line |
|-------|-------------|
| `PORT` is not all digits, or is above 65535 | `invalid PORT "<value>"` |
| The data file exists but cannot be read, or its content is not the layout below (empty, bad JSON, a folder, and so on) | `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>` |
| The port cannot be bound (for example it is in use) | `cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:<port>: <code>` (for example `EADDRINUSE`) |

A missing data file (or a missing folder on its path, `ENOENT`) is not an
error: the server starts with no bookings. After startup the server keeps
running until it is stopped; errors while handling requests are logged to
stderr as `server error: <code>` and answered with 500.

## API

All JSON replies have `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. Every
error reply has the body `{"error": "<message>"}`.

Paths are matched byte for byte against the request target up to the first
`?`: no percent-decoding and no slash, dot-segment or case normalisation
(`/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are not valid routes). The query string is
ignored except for `date` on `GET /api/bookings`.

| Method and path | Success | Errors |
|-----------------|---------|--------|
| `GET /api/rooms` | 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` | |
| `GET /api/bookings` | 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| `POST /api/bookings` | 201, the new booking | 415, 413, 400, 409, 500 (see below) |
| `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` | 204, empty body | 404 `booking not found`, 500 `internal error` |
| `GET /` | 200, the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) | |
| `GET /app.js` | 200, the page script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) | |

Errors that apply to every route:

- Unknown path, any method: 404 `not found`. This includes `/api/bookings/`
  and any `/api/bookings/...` path whose rest contains a `/`.
- Known path with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included):
  405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/1` is 405.
- Any unexpected failure, including a failed save: 500 `internal error`.

### Bookings

A booking has exactly these keys:

```json
{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
```

Ids start at 1 and go up by one. An id is never reused, even after deletes
and restarts.

### `GET /api/bookings`

Returns every booking, sorted by date, then start time, then room (in the
order Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos).

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'
```

With a `date` query parameter, only bookings on that date are returned. The
first `date` value counts if it is repeated, and `?date` with no value counts
as the empty value. A value that is not a valid date (rule 6 below, the empty
value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`.

### `POST /api/bookings`

```sh
curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
```

```
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
{"id":1,"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}
```

Other keys in the body are ignored. The rules are checked in this order, and
the first one that fails decides the reply:

| # | Rule | Reply |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | The `Content-Type` media type (before the first `;`, spaces and tabs trimmed, case ignored) is `application/json` | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
| 2 | The body is at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
| 3 | The body (decoded as UTF-8) parses as a JSON object, not an array, `null`, a string, number or boolean, and is not empty | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
| 4 | `room` is exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case matters) | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
| 5 | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 characters (UTF-16 code units) after trimming whitespace at both ends | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
| 6 | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 (February has 29 days in years divisible by 4) | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| 7 | `start` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
| 8 | `end` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
| 9 | `end` is later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
| 10 | No overlap with a booking of the same room on the same date | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` |

- Only `title` is trimmed, and the booking stores the trimmed title. No other
  field is changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid.
- Two bookings overlap when each starts before the other ends. A booking may
  start exactly when another ends. The 409 message names the start and end of
  the overlapping booking that starts earliest, for example
  `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`.
- Requests that arrive at the same time are handled one at a time: of several
  overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the others get
  409.

### `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`

```sh
curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
```

Replies 204 with an empty body. When `<id>` is not a positive integer in plain
digits without a leading zero (for example `abc`, `01`, `-1`), or no booking
has that id, the reply is 404 `booking not found`.

## Data file

The data file holds one JSON object, written compactly with no trailing
newline:

```json
{"nextId":3,"bookings":[{"id":1,"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}]}
```

- `nextId` is the id the next booking will get. `bookings` is kept in creation
  order; the API sorts on read.
- The file is read once, at startup. It must be exactly this layout: only the
  keys `nextId` and `bookings`; each booking with exactly its six keys and
  valid values (title already trimmed, end after start); ids unique, at least
  1 and below `nextId`; and no two bookings overlapping. Anything else stops
  startup with `cannot read data file <name>`.
- After startup, memory is the source of truth. Changes made to the file from
  outside are not noticed.
- The file is written only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes
  one, and the save finishes before the reply is sent, so a restart with the
  same `DATA_FILE` keeps the bookings and the next id.
- The server never creates folders. If a save fails (for example because the
  file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing
  changes, the next id included. The server keeps running.
- The file is overwritten in place (no temp file). A write that fails partway,
  for example on a full disk, can leave it damaged, and the next startup will
  then refuse it.

## Tests

```sh
npm test             # runs: node --test test/
```

The tests use the built-in `node:test` runner and live in `test/`. They start
`server.mjs` as a child process with `PORT=0` and a temporary `DATA_FILE`, so
they need no free fixed port and do not touch your `bookings.json`.

```
server.mjs        HTTP server, API and data file handling
public/index.html the page (served at /)
public/app.js     the page script (served at /app.js)
test/             node:test tests
package.json      start and test scripts ("type": "module")
```

Only the rooms fetch tests these (`app-load-list.test.mjs:165-171`). 3. **Weak:** Cancel never gets a reply whose body fails later (`replyLater(...).fail()`). Only `fail()` and `replyNotJson(404)` are tested. 4. **Can't be tested:** sorting by "room in the order above". The room names are in alphabetical order, so an alphabetical sort can't be told apart. If a server never listens and never exits, the suite hangs forever. Your mutant runner already passes `--test-timeout=30000`; `npm test` should too. - **Unbounded poll loop.** `startup.test.mjs:172` connects again and again until the child exits, with no upper limit. - **Port races.** `freePort()` binds and releases a port and then hands it to the server (`startup.test.mjs:103` and `:165`). The 3000 and 65535 tests have the same race but skip when the port is busy. The risk is low. - **Fixed delays.** `booking-body.test.mjs:258` waits 300 ms and `persistence.test.mjs:172` waits 100 ms. The suite passes the gate this round: overall 9/10, no item below 8. `npm test` gave 607 pass, 0 fail in about 6 s. I did not re-run the 72 near-miss mutants; that result is your claim.

**What the round 1 fixes changed**
- **Duplication** (6 before) is now 8. The shared helpers in `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/server.mjs` and `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/app.mjs` are used everywhere. `exists` re-throws anything other than ENOENT, and the chunked POST goes through `request({chunks})`. A few small copies are left (listed in the fixes).
- **Order independence** is fixed. The api-list DELETE tests and the booking-fields "201 shape" tests each get their own server. Tests that share a server use `uniqueDate()`, so their bookings never collide.
- **Tests are strong.** Spec messages are matched exactly via `MSG` and `expectError`. Edge cases sit on both sides of each limit: 10000 vs 10001 bytes, multi-byte and chunked bodies, 80 vs 81 title characters with emoji and combining marks, invalid dates, non-Latin digits. Rule order, concurrency, save failures, and the new missing-`public/` 500 test are covered. The fake DOM rejects any API the spec does not allow and logs calls in order, which is how "Book is enabled before anything else" is proved.

**Timeouts: is it enough without `--test-timeout`?** Almost. Every helper wait has a limit except one: `openSocket` sets no socket timeout. So `await ended` in the booking-body "body fully read before reply" tests (lines 223 and 232) would hang forever if the server never closes the connection. Adding a timeout in `openSocket` would close that gap. Otherwise the backend owner needs to add `--test-timeout` to `package.json`.

The few fixed sleeps are acceptable. `delay(300)` in booking-body and `delay(20)`/`delay(100)` in persistence only check that something did *not* happen. Loosening them can only weaken those checks, not make them flaky.

**Other gaps found this round**
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/html.mjs` line 6 still has a raw no-break space in the `nbsp` entry, despite the "invisible characters written as escapes" fix.
- In `booking-fields.test.mjs`, `body()` builds an object and then deletes keys from it. That goes against the "return new objects" standard.

content.text:
The room-booking app is built and its own test suite passes: `npm test` runs 607 tests with none failing. I ran it myself at the end.

The files are `server.mjs`, `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `package.json`, `README.md` and the tests in `test/`.

**What each section did**
- ✅ **backend**: wrote `server.mjs` and `package.json`. The data file is `{"nextId", "bookings"}`, and changes are handled one at a time and saved before memory is updated. Reviewer grade 9/10.
- ✅ **frontend**: wrote the page and its script. The script uses only the browser APIs the spec allows and shows every value as plain text. Grade 9/10.
- ✅ **testing**: wrote the 607 tests, including ones that run the page script against a fake page. It made 72 copies of the code with one plausible bug each, and every copy fails the tests. It found no bugs in the real code. Grade 9/10.
- ❌ **security**: crashed twice. Its built-in security-review step runs `git diff origin/HEAD...`, and this repo has no remote. I went through the security checklist myself by reading the code and found nothing to fix.
- ✅ **docs**: wrote the README: how to start it, the `PORT` and `DATA_FILE` settings, the API, the data file, tests and startup errors.

**Changes from the spec, and stricter readings**
- **Test script:** `npm test` runs `node --test test/*.test.mjs` rather than `node --test test/`. On Node 22.23 the plain folder form fails.
- **Data file check:** the server only accepts exactly the layout it writes itself. Each booking must have valid values, ids must be unique and below the next id, and no two bookings may overlap. Anything else stops startup with `cannot read data file <name>`.
- **Missing file:** only a missing file or folder means "no bookings yet". A path that is a directory, or a file that can't be read, is fatal at startup.
- These and the other two-way readings are logged in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.

**Optional next steps**
- Run the security section again once the repo has a remote.
- Share a few duplicated test helpers.
- Add a `--test-timeout` to the test script as a second guard.

The summary is saved at `.team/reports/2026-11-02/201306-supervisor-summary.md`.
